summary.en-US: Doesn't block ads. Replaces each one with the ad its advertiser would least like you to see.

description.en-US:
Most ad blockers hide ads. Antivertising leaves the space where it is and fills it with the ad its advertiser would least like you to see.

A Pepsi ad becomes a Coke ad. A sportsbook ad becomes an ad for keeping your money. An ad for a car nobody named becomes an ad for the bus.

**How it works**

- It works out who paid for each ad from where the ad leads and what it says, using a built-in list of about 14,000 brands from around the world, matched by their names in English, Japanese and their own languages.
- It picks the replacement that hurts most. That is usually the arch-rival. For gambling, crypto and pay-later ads it is the thing that makes the whole industry pointless.
- It puts that in the ad's place, at the same size. Ads it can't identify get a general heckle, which you can switch off.

**You stay in charge**

- Every card carries a strip saying who paid for the space. Hover it and click **Show original** to get the real ad back.
- The toolbar button counts the swaps on the page, keeps your score and switches the whole thing off.
- **Share** draws a picture of a swap, or of your score, for you to post.

**Private**

- Nothing leaves your browser. There is no server, no account, no analytics and no affiliate links. Rival cards link to the rival's ordinary homepage.
- The add-on keeps a log of the ads it has seen and what replaced them, in your browser only. You can save it as a file, clear it or switch it off.

**The small print**

The replacement ads are parody written for this project. They are not real ads, and no brand named in them has endorsed, paid for or been consulted about any of it. Ads for gambling, lenders and cosmetic clinics are never swapped for a rival's.

The code is open (MIT licence): https://github.com/williamtoner/antivertising

release_notes.en-US: Ads are now swapped the moment they appear, not on a timer, including ads that load late or lower down the page. The built-in list has grown from about 1,500 brands to about 14,000.

version.approval_notes:
Source: the package is exactly the folder extension/ of the public repository https://github.com/williamtoner/antivertising, plus a manifest written by tools/build_firefox.py --listed. It is plain hand-written JavaScript: no build step, no minification, no bundler, no third-party libraries. The only third-party file is the typeface fonts/archivo.woff2 (SIL Open Font License, fonts/OFL.txt). The code is the same as the version self-distributed from the project website under the same number without the final .1; this version differs only in its number and in having no update_url.

What it does: content scripts find ad slots on a page and read each ad's link targets and visible text. The background script works out the advertiser from those, using a brand list shipped in the package (the src/data*.js files, about 14,000 rows of name, colour, domains and rival; they are data, not code fetched from anywhere), and picks a parody card for a rival or an alternative, which the content script puts over the slot. Every card states whose ad it replaced, and Show original on the card restores the real ad. The popup has an off switch.

Network: the add-on sends nothing anywhere. The one fetch() call (src/card.js) loads the bundled font from the package. There is no remote code, no analytics and no data collection. Buttons on the cards are ordinary links to a brand's homepage with no affiliate or tracking parameters. The popup and the share page link to the project website, and Post on X opens x.com's own post page, each only when the user clicks.

Messages between frames: each frame posts two kinds of note to the top frame with window.postMessage, both empty of page content: a random token when it loads (so the top frame can tell which iframe element is which frame) and the fixed string "antivertising:changed" when its document changes (so an ad is swapped when it appears, not on a timer). The top frame's listener stops both before the page's own scripts see them. What a frame's ad actually contains travels only over runtime messaging.

Permissions: host access and webNavigation are used to read ad frames nested inside other frames (webNavigation.getAllFrames, then a message to each frame's content script). storage and unlimitedStorage hold the settings, the score and the ad log (page hostname, ad size, landing domain, up to 400 characters of the ad's text), which the user can export to a file, clear or switch off in the popup. It stays in storage.local.

To test: install, then open https://williamtoner.net/antivertising/test/ . It is a page of nine fake ads, each labelled with what it should turn into. No account or setup is needed.
